summary: Simon Wong is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held a post in Dermatology and Skin Science at the University of British Columbia and was attested as a professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology in 2010.
Singhathon Narāsabho specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Visva-Bharati University, studying under doctoral supervisor Sudhindra Chandra Chakravarti.

Siniruddha Dash is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Director at the University of Madras (2000–2014), the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library (attested 2013), and the K. V. Sarma Research Foundation (2020).

Siran Upendra Deraniyagala (1942–2021) was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin (~1963–1966), the University of London (~1968–1970), and Harvard (~1986–1988), serving as Director General of Archaeology in Sri Lanka (~1992–2001).

Sisir Roy is a philosopher who studied under Debabrata Sensharma. He served as a professor at the Indian Statistical Institute in 1993 and was affiliated with the National Institute of Advanced Studies in 2009.

Sita Krishna Nambiar was an Indologist and philosopher who completed her studies at the University of Bonn under doctoral supervisor Paul Hacker. She later held a post at Indraprastha College for Women.

Sita Ram Roy worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, completing his doctorate under Anant Sadashiv Altekar and Ram Sharan Sharma (1962). He held posts at K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute, Bihar's Directorate of Archaeology, and Gaya Museum.
Siu-tong Kwan is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied under Zhihua Yao and earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.
Sivadatta Sarma was an Indologist who served as a Sanskrit teacher at Maharaja Sanskrit College, Jaipur, with affiliations attested in 1892 and 1929.
Siyong Liang (1904–1954) was an archaeologist and historian. He pursued his education at Tsinghua University and Harvard University, studying at the latter from approximately 1924 to 1930.

Smita Halder is an Indology and history-archaeology scholar studying under doctoral supervisor Susmita Basu Majumdar and holding an appointment as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

So Takahashi (b. 1938) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and Meijo University (associate professor 1977–1978, professor 1991).

Sodo Mori (b. 1934) studied at Komazawa and the University of Tokyo under Hajime Nakamura and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Josai University and Aichi Gakuin University (1991–2003) and served as Pali Text Society's Japanese representative.
Sodo Yokoyama (1907–1980) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Antai-ji (1949–1957) under Kodo Sawaki and Ekō Hashimoto. He taught Joko Shibata.

Soen Nakagawa (1907–1984) was a Buddhist studies figure. He studied at the First Higher School and the University of Tokyo, trained under Gempo Yamamoto (~1931–1961), and taught Robert Baker Aitken, Philip Kapleau, and Maurine Stuart.

Sofija Aleksandrovna Černikova (1936–1995) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the National University of Uzbekistan and the University of Delhi. She taught at the National University of Uzbekistan, becoming a docent in 1970.

Sogaku Harada (1871–1961) was a Buddhist studies master educated at Sendan-Rin School and Komazawa University, where he was a professor (1911–1923). He trained under numerous teachers, including Sotan Oka, and taught Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani.
Sogen Asahina (1891–1979) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Nihon University. He taught at Kanagawa University and instructed Koun Yamada and Kyozo Yamada.

Sogen Omori (1904–1994) was a philosopher and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Nihon University under teachers including Seisetsu Seki. He served as abbot of Koho-in (1947), professor (1970), and president of Hanazono University (1978–1982).

Sogyal Rinpoche (1947–2019) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology teacher who studied at the University of Delhi and Cambridge. Trained by Dudjom Rinpoche and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, among others, he founded Rigpa in 1975.
